title: Battery composition: cohorts, units and uncertainty

steps.title: Check why Table 1 was accepted
steps.question: What kind of measurement does Gate recognize?
steps.look: Gate accepts polymeric and metallic composition fractions for the phone and its components, grouped by manufacturing era.
steps.boundary: Composition is not recovery efficiency. Gate approval alone does not verify every extracted fact.

steps.title: Read the battery polymer fraction
steps.question: What does 23.54 ± 1.42 describe?
steps.look: Table 1 reports the battery polymer fraction for the before-2015 cohort. The extraction separates the value 23.54 from uncertainty 1.42.
steps.boundary: This describes a battery batch, not a catalog model. The uncertainty is retained without inferring its statistical definition.

steps.title: Read the battery metal fraction
steps.question: How much of the battery sample is metallic?
steps.look: The before-2015 battery cell reports 63.01 ± 3.49%. The column identifies the metallic fraction and its manufacturing cohort.
steps.boundary: Total metallic fraction is not a concentration of one element and is not a recovery rate.

steps.title: Keep the other manufacturing cohort separate
steps.question: Can we combine both battery metal measurements?
steps.look: The after-2015 battery metal fraction is 59.46 ± 3.54%. Its different source column keeps it separate from the 63.01% observation.
steps.boundary: Before/after here mean manufacturing eras, not treatment stages. No statistical significance or pooled estimate is inferred.

steps.title: Attach scope: identify the study population
steps.question: Does this observation describe a named phone model?
steps.look: After document merge and revision, Scope adds source context. Scope describes 30 smartphones from nine brands, grouped by manufacturing year before and after 2015. No model was repeated.
steps.boundary: This is batch evidence, not a measurement for a named catalog model. The Scope description is an archived summary. Scope is post-merge provenance, not an upstream extraction input.

steps.title: Follow the battery observation into the final graph
steps.question: What survived normalization?
steps.look: Battery → CONTAINS → Metals retains 63.01%, uncertainty 3.49 and the before-2015 cohort.
steps.boundary: A normalized entity name does not make this batch a specific catalog battery.

steps.title: Retain both cohort observations
steps.question: Are identical endpoints enough to deduplicate?
steps.look: The second Battery → Metals observation retains 59.46%, uncertainty 3.54 and its after-2015 condition.
steps.boundary: Different cohort and cell anchors are distinct measurements even when subject, predicate and object match.

steps.title: Open battery evidence in the fused graph
steps.question: Can we navigate back to the composition cell?
steps.look: Inspect the battery’s CONTAINS observations, choose a metallic fraction, and use View evidence in replay to return to its archived table cell.
steps.boundary: These are composition observations. Catalog battery specifications and treatment recoveries remain different evidence types.
